title: NetBird vs Defguard vs Headscale
summary: Three WireGuard control planes compared for SMB interconnect with Authentik + Coolify. NetBird remains the best mesh fit; Defguard is a hub VPN with connect-time MFA; Headscale is a lean Tailscale-compatible control server.

sections.heading: What each is
bullets: NetBird: full mesh platform (own clients + control plane), P2P WireGuard with relay fallback, routing peers and exit nodes.
Defguard: hub-and-spoke WireGuard remote access + IAM; clients connect to location gateways, not a Tailscale-style any-to-any mesh.
Headscale: open-source Tailscale control server only; uses official Tailscale clients for the data path.

sections.heading: Pros / cons
bullets: NetBird — Pros: mesh for people/servers/sites; first-class Authentik; built-in UI; Coolify netbird-client one-click. Cons: heavier than Headscale; server not one-click on Coolify; HA/SCIM need commercial self-host.

Defguard — Pros: per-connection WireGuard MFA; private Core; enrollment UX; gateway/OPNsense story. Cons: hub-spoke not mesh; external OIDC/Authentik and firewall ACLs need Business tier; no Coolify template; smaller community.

Headscale — Pros: lean; Tailscale client polish; BSD-3; Authentik officially supported; subnet/exit parity with Tailscale base. Cons: no first-party UI; OIDC groups cannot drive ACLs; depends on Tailscale clients; weaker day-2 SMB admin UX.

sections.heading: Recommendation
bullets: 1) NetBird for SMB interconnect + Authentik + Coolify.
2) Headscale if Tailscale clients + minimal control-plane ops matter more than UI.
3) Defguard only if connect-time MFA and classic site gateways outweigh mesh needs.
